# Fantasy and the Thought Life

> "but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart."
>
> — Matthew 5:28

Lust starts in the eyes and the mind, long before it reaches a website or a hand.

Take a man who has quit porn, and means it. He hasn't opened one of those sites in months. He has a red line and he stays on the right side of it.

On the right side of it is every feed of pictures and short videos a phone can show. There are the fitness models, the women trying on clothes for the camera, and the beach photos of a girl he went to school with. None of it would trip a filter. And when the phone is in another room there's the reel in his own head. It holds old girlfriends, scenes he watched years ago, and the woman from the gym.

Perhaps you are that man, and you know how the evening goes. Your partner is tired, or you have no partner, and you feel you're owed something. "I won't look at porn. I'll just scroll for a bit." Forty minutes later you're in the bathroom. Or you don't finish at all, and you go to bed pleased with yourself and wide awake.

Two things make this worse than it looks. First, it props up the belief that you're being deprived. Every swipe tells you that the real feast is over the line and you're a good boy for eating crumbs on the doorstep. Second, it eats your self-respect. An honest man finds himself tilting his screen away from his partner.

## Crumbs are still a meal {-}

The Little Monster doesn't care where his food comes from. Scraps keep him alive as well as a banquet does. The "soft" stuff in your feed gives the itch a moment's ease, which is all it needs to stay awake until next time.

And the feed learns. Pause on one photo for two seconds and it brings you ten more tomorrow. It's a machine for finding your red line and parking you next to it.

The woman on the screen is beautiful. Nobody is denying it. If she were your wife, and in the room, she'd be a gift. But she isn't in the room. She's light on a piece of glass.

A furnace has a pilot light, a tiny flame that burns all day and uses almost no gas. Its only job is to make sure the main burner can fire the instant it's asked. That's what the scroll and the daydream are. You never do it "out of nowhere". The pilot light has been on since breakfast.

## "Then I'll look and not touch" {-}

Hear again what Jesus said: "everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart." He doesn't draw the line at the hand, or at a certain kind of website. He draws it at the gaze.

Notice what he doesn't say. He doesn't say that seeing a beautiful woman is a sin, or that a thought arriving is a sin. A veteran of the recovery forums put the distinction well: "Admiration of beauty is not lust, know the difference." The difference is in three small words: "to lust after". That's a look with a purpose. It's the second look, the lingering one, the one you go back for. Most men know which kind they're doing.

A word for the man who doesn't. Some men get stuck checking whether a look or a thought was a sin, and go round it for hours. If that is you, read this book differently. When you can't tell, treat it as noticing and move on. Don't confess the same thing twice. You will never feel certain, so don't wait to. This kind of checking has a name, scrupulosity. It can be treated, and a doctor or a counselor can help.

For everyone else, be honest about the scroll. It is a purposeful gaze pretending to be an accident.

## You would if you could {-}

Now take the man who has a partner, and still does this to a video, or to the thought of another woman.

Ask what the fantasy is. It's a rehearsal. In his head he has already said yes. Suppose the woman on the screen walked into the room and made the same offer. In the fantasy, he never once says no.

So what is keeping him faithful? It isn't his heart. It's only that she isn't in the room.

Chris Rock, the American comedian, has a hard joke about this. A man, he says, is only as faithful as his options. It gets a big laugh, because every man in the audience knows what he means.

Is that the man you want to be?

**Faithful only because nobody offered.**

This is what Jesus meant by adultery in the heart. He wasn't exaggerating. He was describing a man who would if he could.

Some men will say, "That's not me. I could, and I don't." Then look at why you don't.

There's a man you may recognize. He has a girlfriend, and lately he's been thinking about a ring.

One Friday he's out with friends, and a woman he half knows starts talking to him. She laughs at everything he says. She touches his arm. She isn't really his type. But she's pretty enough for tonight, and he can tell that if he made a move, she would say yes.

He doesn't make one. He walks home feeling rather good about himself. "See? I'm a faithful man."

But he knows why he left, and it wasn't his girlfriend. It was the work. He'd have had to buy the drinks and keep the talk going for another hour. Then there'd be the morning, and her messages, and the lies to keep straight. He never wanted her. He wanted to use her, and using her was too much trouble.

So at home he takes the easy way. He opens his phone and finds a video. Halfway through, it's her face he's thinking of. "Nobody's hurt", he tells himself. "She'll never know."

The next evening his girlfriend is cooking dinner. She looks up, smiles, and asks how his night was. "Quiet", he says.

And a question lands in him that he can't put down. How can she trust a man like this?

She can't. He hasn't touched anyone. But all that stood between her and a betrayal was the bother. He sees it now, and it is not okay.

Your partner deserves better than a man whose loyalty depends on his luck. She deserves a man who wouldn't, even if he could.

That man isn't gritting his teeth. He has stopped wanting it, so there is nothing left to offer him.

## The harem in your head {-}

No filter blocks a memory. That's why some men think the reel is the safe option.

C.S. Lewis didn't. In 1956 a man wrote to him about masturbation. Lewis answered that the habit sends a man back into the prison of himself, to keep a harem of imaginary brides. Here is where he took it. The imaginary women are always available. They never refuse, and they never ask a man to give anything up. So, Lewis wrote, "this harem, once admitted, works against his ever getting out and really uniting with a real woman." A real woman has moods, needs and a mind of her own. The harem has none, so she's the one who starts to feel like hard work.

Then comes his warning: "The danger is that of coming to love the prison."

That's the cost of the thought life. Each time, the cell gets a little more comfortable.

## Taking thoughts captive {-}

So what does a man do with a head like that? Paul, writing to the church in the Greek city of Corinth, gives it one line: "bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ". The picture is a soldier's. A thought turns up, and you don't let it wander where it likes. You take it prisoner. You decide where it goes, and it doesn't decide where you go.

That doesn't mean "try not to think about it". You've tried that, and you know it turns the thought into the biggest thing in the room. An old saying puts it better. You can't stop a bird flying over your head, but you can stop it building a nest in your hair.

The bird is the first thought. It comes by itself, and it is no sin and no failure. The nest is what a man builds out of it afterward.

Watch a nest being built. A man is at the gym, and a woman walks past. He thinks, "She's attractive." That is the bird, and so far nothing has happened. Then he plays it forward in his head. Then he tells himself, "Nobody's hurt. It's only a thought." And tonight, when he is alone, he will feel that he is making a choice. He isn't. The choice was made at the gym, when he let the bird stay.

So the place to act is the beginning, where it costs almost nothing. One man who had broken the habit wrote, "The easiest thought for me to say, 'No' to, is the first one. And if I don't entertain the thought, I'm not going to do it."

That is the whole instruction. Let the bird fly over. Don't build it a nest.

It's far easier than you fear. A man builds the nest for one reason: he believes there's something in it for him. Once he sees that there isn't, the bird comes, finds nowhere to land, and flies on. If you're not a believer, the instruction is the same. Notice the first thought, and let it go by.

## Mothers, sisters, daughters {-}

The feed and the reel are made of women who aren't there. The same eye works on the ones who are: the second look in the next aisle, the conversation at work that runs a little longer than it needs to.

Paul gave a young pastor a rule for this that is hard to improve on. Treat "the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity."

Carry it one step further, and it covers every woman you will ever meet. The older ones are mothers. The ones your own age are sisters. The young ones are daughters.

A man doesn't size up his sister, or perform for her, or keep a door open with her. He doesn't flatter his mother to get something. He would walk through fire for his daughter, and he wants nothing from her at all. He's simply glad they are there.

Imagine living like that for one week, in every shop, office and street. Think how much quieter your head would be.

Here is the funny part. Women can tell the difference at once. Most of them have been looked over by men since they were girls, and they know that look from across a room. A man who talks to them the way he talks to anyone stands out, because he is rare. Don't do it for that. A man who does it to be noticed is back to performing. Just know that it is so.

It changes the woman you're dating as well. Nothing is wrong with wanting a beautiful wife. But beauty can blind a man, and a blind man signs anything. So take her face out of the question for a minute, and ask two plain things. Do I really like being with her? Can I build a life with her? A man ruled by lust can't answer those. He has never been calm enough near her to find out.

A free man can.

## The app {-}

The feed has a cousin, and it looks respectable. It's the dating app.

There is nothing wrong with wanting a wife, or with meeting her through a phone. Plenty of good marriages began that way. But be honest about why you open it. A man looking for a wife reads slowly and writes to one woman. A thirsty man swipes. He goes through fifty faces in five minutes and sorts each one in half a second. What he's after is the small jolt when one of them matches.

One man told a newspaper that he swiped yes on every woman the app showed him. At his worst he was talking to ten at once. He wasn't looking for any of them. He wanted to know that women found him attractive.

Another man made it plainer still. He had been on one app for eight years. Then he met a woman at a party, and they decided to get married. He wrote on a forum that he was still swiping, though he never spoke to a single match. He had what the app was supposed to be for, and he couldn't put it down. Somebody answered him, "Don't you get it? You won!"

That is the same itch in better clothes. The swipe is the scroll, with a chance attached.

So the test is simple. Are you looking for a wife, or looking for a hit? If it's a wife, you won't need fifty at a time. If it's a hit, you know what to call it.

## The one girl {-}

The app is fifty faces. The opposite case is one.

You check your phone forty times an hour. You've read her last message until you know it by heart, and you write your answer five times before you send it. You know when she was last online. It feels like love. It even feels like the opposite of the harem, because she is one woman and she is real.

Look closer. You aren't thinking about her. You're thinking about what you want from her, and about how you look to her. What you care about is the feeling you have for her, and the longing. She has become a picture in your head, and you're texting the picture. It's the harem with one face in it.

A free man can like a woman, tell her so plainly, and get on with his day while he waits for her answer. If she says no, he's sorry, and he is still himself. That's the kind of man a woman can say yes to.

## The pictures {-}

One more thing passes between a man and the girl on his mind, and that is pictures. You ask her for one, or you send one of yourself and hope. Be honest about what you're doing. You are making your own porn, with a woman you know. You've turned her into something to look at before you have learned who she is. And a picture, once sent, belongs to whoever holds the phone. A free man doesn't ask for it. If she offers, he says no, and she will remember that he did.

## Seeing people again {-}

Here is what waits on the other side. NoFap is an online movement of men who give up porn and masturbation. One of them, a hundred days out, noticed that the women around him had changed. Of course it was his eyes that had changed. He had stopped scanning their bodies, he wrote, and "started noticing much more interesting things about them. Smiles, gestures". He was seeing people again.

Set him beside the man who quit porn and kept the feed. That man is still standing at his red line, with a phone full of crumbs and a head full of women who aren't there.

AND HE CALLS IT BEING FREE!
